action: If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis, move funds to a new wallet with a new seed, stop using the device and contact Trezor Support via trezor.io/support for a replacement. Buy only from trezor.io.
exec: A physical supply-chain tamper at a hardware-wallet reseller shows that firmware integrity alone does not protect devices bought through third parties.
plain: Three Trezor crypto wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller had a hidden chip that steals the secret recovery words. Trezor has released a fix and is replacing devices.
summary: Trezor said on November 12 that three Safe 5 wallets bought from Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis between August 20 and September 23, including via its Tokopedia and Shopee stores, held an added circuit board that copies what the screen shows and sends recovery words over the mobile network. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the current implants. Forty-eight customers have come forward for checks.
title: Trezor confirms seed-stealing hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by reseller CryptoBilis

validation.note: Vendor's own investigation post; BleepingComputer's front page carries the same finding.

review.note: Trezor post Nov 12: three Safe 5, Aug 20-Sep 23, Tokopedia/Shopee, firmware 2.13.1, 48 customers match.
